answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and that deposit is slashed if peers prove it duplicated itself or faked work. Like an inlet that only admits boats through one narrow channel, the network forces each identity through a costly gate, so spawning thousands of copies becomes expensive. Reputation accrues slowly, like umber pigment deepening over time, while a fresh zephyr of new accounts carries no weight until it has done verified work over many epochs. Sybils can still appear, but they cannot cheaply outvote honest agents.
